think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A young woman from an endemic region presents with medically refractory focal epilepsy and recurrent episodes of perilesional edema around a calcified brain lesion, despite negative serum serology. Calcified parasitic lesions were traditionally considered inert scars; however, episodic perilesional edema with cyclical ring enhancement represents a recognized mechanism of refractory breakthrough seizures in parenchymal neurocysticercosis, frequently misdiagnosed as glioma or cavernoma.
2. Admission Breakpoint: History of migrating from India, chronology of focal motor seizures, initial CT finding of a left frontal calcified fleck with ring enhancement, and MRI demonstrating a persistent calcified signal void with fluctuating perilesional edema and seizure clusters mark the admission breakpoint prior to stereotactic craniotomy and histopathology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Low-grade glial neoplasm or oligodendroglioma (causes focal seizures with calcification, but serial imaging shows stable calcified core with fluctuating non-neoplastic edema rather than tumor progression), Intracranial tuberculoma (major cause of solitary ring-enhancing lesions in India, but typically forms caseating solid granulomas rather than an involuting calcified cyst), and calcified Neurocysticercosis granuloma with recurrent perilesional inflammation.
case_prompt: A right-handed adolescent female originally from India who migrated to Malaysia presented with medically refractory focal seizures. At age 9 in India, she experienced an initial simple partial seizure characterized by clonic shaking of her right hand lasting one minute. A computed tomography (CT) brain scan at that time demonstrated a hyperdense calcified focus ('white fleck') in the left frontal lobe with ring enhancement and surrounding edema. Carbamazepine was initiated, but she suffered a second seizure two months later while traveling in Sweden; serum serological testing was negative. Seven months later, follow-up CT demonstrated persistence of the left frontal calcified focus, but the edema had completely resolved. After remaining seizure-free on carbamazepine for 19 months with a normal EEG, the medication was gradually tapered and discontinued. Following nearly two years of remission, she had a third seizure. Brain MRI revealed a susceptibility signal void in the left frontal lobe with contrast ring enhancement and perilesional vasogenic edema. Despite antiepileptic treatment with levetiracetam, she developed an acute cluster of four focal motor seizures over four consecutive days. A repeat brain MRI demonstrated persistent left frontal signal void with marked recrudescence of contrast ring enhancement and increased perilesional edema.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Low-grade cerebral neoplasm / Ganglioglioma / Cavernous malformation
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Focal cortical calcification presenting with medically refractory motor seizures in a young person raises suspicion for a low-grade tumor or vascular malformation; however, long-term neuroimaging showed a stationary calcified core with fluctuating perilesional inflammatory edema rather than a progressive expansile neoplasm, and surgical pathology showed no neoplastic cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A computed tomography (CT) brain scan at that time showed a white fleck in the left frontal lobe with ring enhancement and surrounding edema.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Tuberculomas are the leading cause of solitary ring-enhancing granulomas in the Indian subcontinent; however, the lesion demonstrated a dense punctate calcified core with cyclical episodic perilesional edema rather than expanding caseation, and histology confirmed a necrotic cystic cavity surrounded by gliosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) brain scan showed a signal void in the left frontal lobe with ring enhancement on contrast imaging and perilesional edema.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot (Calcified Neurocysticercosis Granuloma with Perilesional Edema)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Stereotactic craniotomy and resection of the epileptogenic calcified lesion revealed an encapsulated cystic structure surrounded by gliotic parenchyma containing necrotic parasitic remnants, confirming an involuted calcified Taenia solium metacestode causing recurrent perilesional inflammatory edema and intractable seizures.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histological assessment showed a cystic structure surrounded by gliotic brain. It was entirely necrotic except for several small oval structures but no scolex or cuticle with spines (features of a tapeworm). The histological picture was suggestive of a necrotic parasite, unclassified.

editor_comments: Compelling case illustrating that calcified neurocysticercosis lesions are not biologically inert, but can cause refractory epilepsy via episodic antigen release and perilesional edema. Admission prompt cleanly details the imaging chronology without revealing histopathologic confirmation.
